clue.text: Battle remembered in the long run

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a battle will be remembered in the long run.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses joined by 'in': the battle of 490 BC, remembered through the race named after the runner's legendary dash to Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Marathon was the Greek victory over Persia, and the 26-mile road race takes its name from it.

clue.text: Cook flared, blamed for burning cakes

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify or rework them, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook flared up, angry at being blamed for some burnt cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the person in the kitchen; it is the anagram signal working on 'flared'.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the Saxon king, hiding in a peasant's hut, let her cakes burn and was scolded for it.

clue.text: Stay in Lincoln — I would

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: Abe is the familiar first name of US president Abraham Lincoln
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: Someone says they would happily stay in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city; it is the president, ABE, with ID set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to remain or stay somewhere, as in 'abide with me'.

clue.text: It's a shame having to eat it

definitions.text: It's a shame having to eat it

parts.words: It's a shame having to eat it
parts.note: the dish in the idiom for being forced into an embarrassing apology

explanation.definitionFit: Eating it means being humiliated into admitting a mistake, a shameful climbdown.

clue.text: Certainly it's not far eastern in origin

indicators.note: the word eastern is the origin from which the answer's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that something is certainly not from the Far East in origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not far eastern' tempts a reading about the Far East, but 'eastern' is the fodder, reshuffled as signalled by 'in origin'.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of near describes whatever is least distant, certainly not far.

clue.text: Almost ready to include me in the cure

indicators.note: to include means one piece takes another inside it
almost tells us the word ready falls a letter short of complete

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's remedy is almost ready, and the patient asks to be included in the cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the A of READY, leaving REDY; 'to include' puts ME inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a treatment that heals, a synonym for cure.

clue.text: Assessed speed on start of descent

parts.note: rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

indicators.note: start of picks out the opening letter of the word descent

explanation.surface: An examiner judged the speed at the start of a downhill run.
explanation.definitionFit: Rated means evaluated or judged, a synonym for assessed.

clue.text: Dives for coins a great deal

explanation.surface: A diver plunges for coins and gathers a great haul of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives is the rich man in Jesus's parable of Lazarus, a name for any wealthy person; 'for' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich man is called this, and the phrase also literally means sacks holding plenty of cash.

clue.text: Store fish — for the stew?

parts.note: a dump is a store or depot, as in an ammunition dump
ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone stores fish, perhaps planning to put it in a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A suet ball cooked on top of a casserole is a classic addition to a stew.

clue.text: State in a loud and resolute way

parts.note: f, for forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
firm means steadfast or resolute

explanation.surface: Advice to state something loudly and with conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to declare or assert something as true.

clue.text: May out on spree showing independence

indicators.note: a spree is a wild outing, so the letters of may out on run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: May goes out on a spree to show she is her own woman.
explanation.walkthrough: May reads as a woman's name; with OUT and ON it is the fodder, shuffled as 'spree' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Autonomy is self-government or freedom from outside control.

clue.text: The militant's first summons

parts.note: the bugle call that wakes soldiers, the first order of the military day

explanation.definitionFit: The morning bugle call rouses troops at daybreak, their first call of the day.

clue.text: Such fishermen bring the catch to the surface

definitions.text: Such fishermen bring the catch to the surface

parts.words: Such fishermen bring the catch to the surface
parts.note: anglers whose artificial lure floats on the water, so the fish rises up to take it

explanation.definitionFit: This kind of angling uses a floating artificial insect, so the trout comes up to the top to bite.

clue.text: Head profits from a form of taxation

parts.note: capital means head, from Latin caput, as in a capital letter heading a line
gains are profits

explanation.surface: The head of a firm takes profits from a type of tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit made on selling an asset is taxed separately in Britain, giving its name to a levy.

clue.text: It comes from Mecca, this religious instruction

indicators.note: the answer comes from the letters of Mecca this rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that this piece of religious teaching originates in Mecca.
explanation.walkthrough: Mecca suggests Islam, but the answer is the Christian question-and-answer teaching; its letters come from MECCA THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is a summary of doctrine taught by question and answer.

clue.text: Live broadcast about it, with something witty as theme

indicators.note: about means going around, so the shuffled letters surround the other pieces
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of live are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a mot, as in bon mot, is a witty remark

explanation.surface: A live broadcast about something, with a clever remark as its theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns LIVE into LE...IV; 'about' wraps it round IT and MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a recurring musical or literary motif, a theme associated with a character or idea.

clue.text: I'm off food and water

parts.note: fare means food, as on a bill of fare
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are giving up food and water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm off' looks like someone going without; it is a parting word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is said when departing, the same as goodbye.

clue.text: Contest for comedians?

parts.note: comedians are wits, so a contest between them is a clash of clever people

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a sharp exchange of cleverness, read literally as a fight between jokers.

clue.text: Squander food?

explanation.surface: Is it wasteful to spend on food?
explanation.walkthrough: One word as a verb means waste, and as a noun a battered fried snack such as an apple one.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter away money is to waste it, and a fritter is a piece of battered fried food.

clue.text: Food taken from the hand

parts.note: fruit growing in a bunch called a hand, picked from it one finger at a time

explanation.definitionFit: This fruit grows in clusters called hands, each fruit a finger.

clue.text: One who foils trespassers?

parts.note: a fighter with a foil, the sword, read as someone who thwarts intruders by putting up a barrier

explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman wielding a foil, the light sword, also suggests someone who builds barriers against intruders.

clue.text: Work to rule?

parts.note: the industrial protest phrase read literally as the job of ruling as a monarch

explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period on the throne is spent governing, literally working at ruling.

clue.text: I'm only human but never to be forgotten

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a mortal is someone merely human, bound to die

explanation.surface: Someone protests they are only human, yet hope to be remembered for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Immortal means living for ever, so famous enough to be remembered eternally.

clue.text: Either way it's essential to a helicopter

indicators.note: either way says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A remark that, whichever way you look at it, this part is vital to a chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning blade assembly gives a helicopter its lift.

clue.text: Female freedom fighter

parts.note: read as a guerrilla, but meaning a campaigner for women's liberation

explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner for women's rights fights for their liberation.

clue.text: It returns more than once to an old master

indicators.note: more than once says the turned piece appears twice
returns means the word it comes back the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something keeps going back to an old master painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns IT into TI, 'more than once' doubles it to TITI, then AN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great sixteenth-century Venetian painter, one of the Old Masters.

clue.text: Congenial address for a ship's captain?

explanation.surface: A friendly way to speak to the skipper of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' links two senses: the chummy British form of address between friends, and sailors' slang for the captain.
explanation.definitionFit: British men call a friend this affectionately, and crews call their skipper the same.

clue.text: Defeat makes no difference to mum or dad

definitions.text: makes no difference to mum or dad

explanation.surface: Losing a match does not change things for one's parents.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum and dad read the same backwards, so turning them round leaves them as they were.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback or defeat is called this, and the act of turning words backwards leaves palindromes unchanged.
